items.actClause:
AN ACT to require the empire state development corporation to create a plan
regarding multi-use trails
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4416

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to require the empire state development corpo-
ration to create a plan regarding multi-use trails

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

AN ACT to require the empire state development corporation to create a
plan regarding multi-use trails

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS: Section 1:

(a) Defines a multi-use trail as "an off-street linear facility for
recreation and transportation, paved or unpaved, designated to serve
multiple types of users, including, but not limited to, bicyclists,
pedestrians, in-line skaters, joggers, cross-country skiers or equestri-
ans"

(b) Directs the Empire State Development Corporation (EDC) to create a
plan for a comprehensive statewide system of multi-use trails.
Describes drafting, review and agency input. Identifies specific parame-
ters of the plan.

(c) Describes the role of other agency stakeholders.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Multi-use trails have been observed to have an important economic impact
on the communities around them, with the Erie Canalway Trail alone
having an estimated impact of $253 million in sales, 3,440 jobs, $78
million in labor income, and $28.5 million in tax revenue.  This effect
stands to be multiplied in New York State, with the impending
construction of the new Empire State Trail. Additionally, New York has
more than 1,000 miles of regional and local trails networks found all
across the state. While these trails enhance their communities, their
economic impact is stymied by a lack of long term planning.

In order to advance trail development to their full potential, and maxi-
mize the various benefits of trails, New York needs a coordinated strat-
egy for linking existing and potential individual trail corridors to
create a statewide, interconnected system. With thousands of miles of
scenic rivers and streams, lakeshores, canals, historic roadways, and
abandoned railroad corridors, plus hundreds of appealing cities, towns
and villages,òopportunities to create additional trails and connections
between existing trails abound in every region of the state.

A 10-year plan to build out the connectivity of regional trail networks
will enhance the economic impact of existing trails and the new Empire
State Trail and will create more opportunities for outdoor recreation,
tourism and health benefits in every corner of New York.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

B.actClause:
AN ACT to require the office of parks, recreation and historic preservation to
create a plan regarding non-motorized multi-use trails
B.lawSection: Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation Law
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4416B

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to require the office of parks, recreation and
historic preservation to create a plan regarding non-motorized multi-use
trails

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation would require OPRHP to create a plan regarding non-mo-
torized multi use trails.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: The Office of Parks, Recreation, and Historic Preservation
shall create a plan for a comprehensive statewide system of non-motor-
ized multi-use trails within one year of the effective date.  Parks
shall consult with DEC, DOH and DOT to create such plan. These individ-
uals shall meet quarterly. This section requires a 60 day public comment
period and at a minimum one public hearing on the draft plan during that
time. The plan shall be updated at a minimum every five years.

Specifically the plan shall include a vision for a statewide network of
non-motorized primary corridors linked to and enhanced by regional and
local non-motorized trails with goals for geographic distribution, and
universal accessibility. Also requires a geographic information system
inventory of existing non-motorized multi-use trails, as well as planned
trails or undeveloped corridors under consideration. The plan shall
identify new non-motorized multi-use trail opportunities, as well as
recommend funding. Section 2 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Non-Motorized multi-use trails have been observed to have an important
economic impact on the communities around them, with the Erie Canalway
Trail alone having an estimated impact of $253 million in sales, 3,440
jobs, $78 million in labor income, and $28.5 million in tax revenue.
This effect stands to be multiplied in New York State, with the impend-
ing construction of the new Empire State Trail.  Additionally, New York
has more than 1,000 miles of regional and local trails networks found
all across the state. While these trails enhance their communities,
their economic impact is stymied by a lack of long term planning.

In order to advance trail development to their full potential, and maxi-
mize the various benefits of trails, New York needs a coordinated strat-
egy for linking existing and potential individual trail corridors to
create a statewide, interconnected system. With thousands of miles of
scenic rivers and streams, lakeshores, canals, historic roadways, and
abandoned railroad corridors, plus hundreds of a appealing cities, towns
and villages, opportunities to create additional trails and connections
between existing trails abound in every region of the state.

A plan to build out the connectivity of regional trail networks will
enhance the economic impact of existing trails and the new Empire State
Trail and will create more opportunities for outdoor recreation, tourism
and health benefits in every corner of New York.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

summary: Requires the office of parks, recreation and historic preservation to create a plan regarding non-motorized multi-use trails in consultation with the department of environmental conservation, the department of health and the department of transportation.
